answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to prove elapsed computation through a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every result depending on the one before it. GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot divide one chain’s sequential steps to skip its delay; creating many identities therefore takes parallel hardware and real time. A verifier checks each VDF proof efficiently, while every kernel must complete its own work: a ripple of cloned identities cannot flow past the bottleneck like a river.
